title: Durable job journal paired native evaluation
note: This paired native run compares clean built base 2a3a0647ec25eb66b906aab1be7db9f400bd0ce1 with clean built candidate 69158ef2676452ad237587bf4b3c650eebd2aa54. It retains all 324 unique samples: eight standard scenarios plus background_test, three trials, and six available standard/extended-set models. No samples are invalid or excluded. Five candidate models pass all 27 tasks; GPT passes 24/27 in both arms. All six GPT failures are malformed edit streams stopped by the whitespace guard. The seventh failure is a base Sonnet background_test that ran the waiting check in the foreground and reached its 60-second tool timeout; this is a model choice, not evidence that the journal caused the outcome. The seven failed samples lack complete usage and remain in failure counts. No regression rule is flagged. Token and request differences include model variability and distinct binary paths; this record establishes no causal efficiency gain. Gemini tool errors on successful tasks are git inspection outside a repository; the base additionally records expected failing tests before repair. The required gemini-3.8-flash-medium route was unavailable; the owner approved gemini-3.8-flash-high at high effort. That substitution leaves required medium coverage missing. The runner uses --no-session, so it exercises live job/tool flow but cannot qualify crash durability or recovery; separate real child-kill/reopen tests prove started-before-producer, terminal-before-publication, and observation-before-acknowledgement ordering. The candidate full preflight passed all 35 gates. macOS was attempted but SSH authentication failed before checks. These samples do not measure the later shared RunControl, typed task documents, or background compaction changes.

settings.effort: medium where the model offers it; DeepSeek runs at high, its default, having no medium

regressionRule: all tasks, per model: total tokens with the 95% interval above zero; requests up more than 10% with the 95% interval above zero; failures +2 or more; any tool-error increase
